children: Indu Bhan New Delhi: The Supreme Court has ruled that a Committee of Creditors (CoC) cannot withdraw its approval given to a resolution plan after the same has been placed before the National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) for approval even if the debt-laden company's financial position has improved considerably.

A bench of justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran disposed of the appeal filed by Bank of India and other CoC members, including Canara Bank, India Infrastructure Finance, Union Bank of India, UCO Bank and Punjab National Bank. The bench said the resolution plan remains binding on the CoC and the successful resolution applicant (SRA).

An improvement in the corporate debtor's profitability alone cannot be grounds for refusing approval if the plan meets the requirements of the IBC. It noted that a resolution plan is not an ordinary contract, but approved through the statutory framework of the IBC, including the voting mechanism under Section 30(4), under which even dissenting creditors are bound.

However, the bench directed the tribunal to consider together the application seeking approval of the resolution plan and the holding company's application seeking implementation of a one-time settlement and an end to the corporate insolvency resolution process. In the case of Bank of India vs SM Kamal Pasha, the CoC had unanimously decided to withdraw the resolution plan as TD Toll Road's financial position had substantially improved during the years when the resolution professional was in management.

The lenders argued that permitting the plan to proceed would give the SRA a windfall as it would have to bring in significantly less fresh funding than contemplated when the resolution plan was submitted. The opening balance had risen from about 30 crore at the time of the resolution plan to 165 crore by the time the Supreme Court concluded the proceedings by dismissing the appeal filed by the erstwhile promoter.

title: CoC Cannot Withdraw Resolution Plan Post NCLT Filing: Apex Court
